biography: Roland Rohrer, born amidst the picturesque Austrian Alps, didn't inherit racing; he discovered it. While working as a ski instructor in his late teens, the roar of a rally car echoing through the mountains ignited a passion he couldn't ignore. He traded his skis for a steering wheel, initially competing in local hill climbs with a battered, second-hand Lada. His raw talent quickly became apparent, attracting the attention of a small, regional rally team. Rohrer's aggressive, yet calculated, driving style proved effective, quickly earning him a reputation as a rising star. A defining moment arrived at the 2021 Schneeberg Rally, where, despite a near-catastrophic collision with a snowbank, he recovered to clinch victory in the final stage. Currently, Rohrer finds himself at the peak of his career, campaigning with the Mitsubishi Lancer RX team, aiming to establish himself as a force to be reckoned with on the international rallycross stage. He is known for his meticulous preparation and calm demeanor, but also for his fierce competitiveness on the track.
drivingStyle: Rohrer's driving style is best described as 'defensive aggression'. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes or risky maneuvers. Instead, he focuses on consistent lap times, minimizing errors, and exploiting any weaknesses in his opponents' lines. He's incredibly adept at managing tire wear, often preserving his rubber for the final laps when others are struggling for grip. Under pressure, Rohrer becomes even more calculated, rarely cracking under duress. He prefers to maintain a steady pace, forcing his rivals to make mistakes rather than initiating high-risk moves himself.

rivalries.reason: Herrera's aggressive, flamboyant style clashes directly with Rohrer's calculated approach, leading to several on-track incidents and heated exchanges in the paddock.
Petrova and Rohrer have a long-standing rivalry stemming from their junior rally days. She consistently outmaneuvers him on technical courses, fueling his determination to outperform her.
Tanaka's stoic personality mirrors Rohrer's, leading to an intense, almost unspoken rivalry based on pure skill and determination.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of faded blue driving gloves, a gift from his grandfather.
Listens to classical music (specifically Mozart) for an hour before every race to calm his nerves.
Meticulously cleans and polishes his helmet visor before each session, regardless of weather conditions.
famousQuote: Victory isn't about taking risks; it's about minimizing them.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2023 European Rallycross Championship after a season-long battle, securing the title with a daring last-corner pass in the final race at Höljes.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2022 World Rallycross Championship in Cape Town due to a mechanical failure, costing him a potential world title.
